H_proposal.falsifier: Refuted (and demoted, keeping the base procedure for that component) if any of: F1 a design that passes every certificate inequality with the stated margins still ends with packets=[] or a tx-transient / energy-threshold brownout before tx-complete, or tx-complete after deadline_s or beyond max_data_age_s; F2 the certificate does not flag the retained design (C=50e-6, tx_not_before=2) as violated, i.e. it cannot explain the retained failure; F3 a design that clearly violates the energy or ceiling inequality (e.g. emax < E_tx + eoff) nevertheless yields a valid 8-byte frame, showing the derived accounting is wrong for the frozen model; F4 the maximin selection rule produces no admissible point at all in the legal ranges while a non-maximin point in the same ranges would have been admissible. Any single observation above falsifies the size/placement of the margins, not the frozen task, evaluator or model.
H_proposal.hypothesis: The retained failure is an energy-budget violation, not a gating/protocol defect. Under the frozen law, one transmit step costs V_out*I_tx*dt = 25 uJ and a full 2-step frame costs 50 uJ, while the retained design (C=50uF, tx_not_before=2) began TX at the capture instant with stored energy ~25 uJ (eon = C*V_ready^2/2), so the second step's post-draw energy fell below eoff = 1 uJ and the model emitted brownout(tx-transient); because event_latch is volatile the only capture was cleared and no later contact exists, so packets stayed empty. Therefore a design procedure that (i) derives a closed-form feasibility certificate (boot-before-event, TX energy incl. per-step voltage floor and post-TX eoff, storage ceiling emax, timing/deadline) from component_record + excitation_record + model_law BEFORE spending candidate executions, (ii) treats C as two-sided (small enough to boot before the 1 ms event, large enough that emax can hold E_tx+eoff and cross the V_out floor), and (iii) maximin-selects margins instead of choosing the earliest legal TX gate, will analytically flag the retained design as infeasible and raise the chance that a single 8-byte frame completes inside [event_s, deadline_s]. This is a procedural revision of H only; it asserts no hardware result, no statistical advantage, no migration and no RSI.
H_proposal.method_text:
M-H2: energy-budget-gated design procedure (volatile latch, single-frame deadline). Read-only derivation first; device parameters are outputs of the procedure, not inputs to it.

Step 0 -- facts, no execution. From component_record, excitation_record, model_law and saved_activity record: legal C range and tx_not_before range; event_s, contact_duration_s, deadline_s, dt_s; source segments (power_w, start/end), harvest_efficiency, shunts; boot_j, boot_delay_s, idle_power_w, off_power_w; output_v (V_out), tx_current_a (I_tx), tx_duration_s (T_tx), ready_v, off_v, cap_voltage_max_v, event_latch type; required_application_bytes and unique_frames. Never edit these facts, the model, the ranges or the query token.

Step 1 -- derived quantities (symbolic, per candidate C). eon = C*V_ready^2/2; eoff = C*V_off^2/2; emax = C*V_max^2/2; e_floor = C*V_out^2/2 (draw-time voltage floor); N = ceil(T_tx/dt); E_step = V_out*I_tx*dt; E_tx = V_out*I_tx*T_tx; P_net = harvest_efficiency*sum(source power over the pre-event interval) - background power, using the pessimistic (higher) background and crediting no harvest that is not in the record.

Step 2 -- pre-execution feasibility certificate. A candidate (C, tx_not_before) is admissible only if every line holds WITH an explicit stated margin (report the margin value per line, never a bare pass/fail):
 (a) powered-in-time: t_boot(C) = (eon + boot_j)/P_net + boot_delay_s + 2*dt must be < event_s - dt. Rationale: with a volatile latch the 1 ms contact is captured only while powered; a late boot loses the event irrecoverably. (Retained design satisfied this: first_boot_s = 1.316 < 2.0.)
 (b) TX energy budget: e_need(C) = max(e_floor + (N-1)*E_step, E_tx + eoff); require stored energy at TX start e_s >= e_need + safety, with safety = max(E_step, 0.2*e_need), because a reset between tx-start and tx-complete destroys the only frame and no second contact exists.
 (c) storage ceiling: emax >= e_need + safety. If the capacitor cannot physically hold E_tx + eoff plus the step floor, that C is infeasible, not merely marginal.
 (d) timing window: t_tx >= max(tx_not_before, t_reach(e_need + safety)) with t_reach ~= e_need/P_net; t_tx + T_tx <= deadline_s - 2*dt; t_tx - event_s <= max_data_age_s.
 (e) per-step replay: for j = 1..N, pre-draw energy e_s - (j-1)*E_step >= e_floor, and post-draw final energy e_s - E_tx >= eoff + safety/2. Never let float equality at a threshold be load-bearing.

Step 3 -- selection rule (maximin, not single-knob maximization). F = {C in range: (a),(b),(c) hold} intersected with {tx_not_before in range: (d),(e) hold}. Choose the point maximizing the minimum normalized margin over (a),(b),(c),(d),(e). Explicitly forbid the two attractors seen in the retained record: the smallest legal tx gate (fires at the capture instant with no stored packet energy) and the largest legal C (delays boot past the contact and raises eon/e_floor).

Step 4 -- order of experiments (within the registered budget). (4.1) Re-derive the retained failure analytically and require the certificate to reject it: C = 50e-6, tx_not_before = 2 gives e_s ~ 25e-6 = eon, step-1 draw 25e-6 leaves ~0 < eoff, so the model's reset fires and volatile capture is cleared -> violated (b)/(e). If the certificate cannot reject the retained point, stop and keep the base procedure. (4.2) Spend at most the registered candidate executions on the maximin admissible point first, then on one off-center admissible point chosen to make the boot-before-event line (a) binding, to test whether (a) or (b) is the true constraint. Do not use an execution to test a point the certificate already rejects.

Step 5 -- observation policy and retention. Judge each execution from per-step trace fields (stored_j, loaded_v, powered, event_captured) plus activity (boot, capture, tx-start, tx-complete, brownout reason) and packets (exactly one frame, application_bytes = required_application_bytes, distinctness), and convert tx-complete time to seconds versus event_s and deadline_s. Retain every failure, unknown and cost verbatim. No acceptance claim: the host's independent service decides, and physical calibration stays UNKNOWN.

Step 6 -- update discipline. On a failed candidate change one item only (one margin constant or one inequality) and re-derive; if certificate prediction and observed outcome disagree, presume the certificate (not the frozen model) is wrong and weaken it rather than adding new constraints. Keep the base method for any component with no supporting observation.

Also falsified if an executed point with strictly negative derived margin nevertheless emits a valid 8-byte packet, which would show the derived inequalities are not necessary. UNKNOWN/failed outcomes are retained verbatim, never converted into a success claim.
H_proposal.hypothesis: The retained base failure is a device-level energy-budget failure at the transmit step, not a capture or timing failure, and it is repairable by an eval-derived procedure rather than by a guessed parameter. Mechanism readable from the acquired sources: with the volatile latch, capture requires being powered at the single contact step t=2.000; the recorded law spends output_v*tx_current*dt=25 uJ in each 1 ms step and resets ('tx-transient') whenever sqrt(2*E_before/c)-esr*I < output_v or E_after < eoff. At the base point the pre-transmit store is only ~38 uJ, so the second step collapses to ~0.72 V. Hypothesis: the necessary pre-transmit store is E*(c)=max(n*tx_j+eoff, (n-1)*tx_j+eon) with n=ceil(tx_duration/dt)=2, and a design point is deliverable iff emax>=E*, eon<=E_avail(contact), and completion<=deadline with data age<=max_data_age_s; therefore a procedural derivation over the legal grid (not a fixed assignment) recovers a non-empty window containing the unchanged capacitance. Scope is the frozen ideal digital BF apparatus with synthetic waveforms; physical calibration, real latch persistence and any datasheet energy claim remain UNKNOWN and are not asserted.
H_proposal.method_text:
SCOPE AND ROLES. This is a procedural (H) update only, consumed from task entry, for the frozen ideal digital BF apparatus (world clite-query-window-derived-v1, partition public-development). The component record describes synthetic waveform assumptions; physical calibration, real latch persistence and databook energy claims are UNKNOWN and are never asserted here. This interface has no device check: no acceptance is claimed, and no device assignment is presented as the method. Separate the two artifacts explicitly: D = the device record and its legal parameters (capacitance_f in [2.5e-5,1e-4], tx_not_before_s in [2,7]) plus anything the host executes; H = method, observation policy, experiment order, context policy. The update below changes H only. Any coupled D change must be executed by the host and fed back COMPLETELY (full per-step trace fields stored_j, voltage_v, loaded_v, tx_j, spill_j, background_j, powered, contact, event_captured; full activity list; full packets list; the executed parameter pair; the source version hashes); no partial or summarized feedback is accepted as evidence.

SOURCE-BOUND READING (do this before proposing anything). Build every quantity from the acquired payloads only, using the recorded model law as the authority for ordering: per step, e += power_w*dt*harvest_efficiency; spill = max(0, e - c*cap_voltage_max_v^2/2); e -= min(e, (idle_power_w if powered else off_power_w)*dt); then resets; then boot when not powered and e >= eon = c*ready_v^2/2; then, only if powered and t >= ready_at, capture when the contact interval holds, and the transmit branch when captured and t >= tx_not_before_s. Note ordering consequences: the transmit branch can fire on the SAME step as capture, the per-step debit is output_v*tx_current_a*min(dt, tx_left), and the loaded-voltage test uses the pre-debit store. Contact is the single step satisfying event_s <= t < event_s + contact_duration_s (here one step, because contact_duration_s equals dt_s). Resets come in exactly two families, 'energy-threshold' and 'tx-transient'; with a volatile latch a reset clears the capture flag and after a completed transmit the flag is also cleared. Therefore report service completion (a frame actually emitted) separately from any statement about pending-state retention: holding the captured flag while powered is retention-while-powered only, and is NOT evidence that the pending state survives a reset.

FAILURE LOCALIZATION (applied to the retained observation). Boot at 1.316 s equals 25 uJ / 0.019 uJ per ms, so the recorded law and the recorded activity agree; capture at 2.000 s and a transmit start on the same step follow from tx_not_before_s = 2 <= t; the first debit of 25 uJ leaves about 13 uJ, giving loaded_v about 0.72 V < output_v on the next step; the reset reason recorded is 'tx-transient', which is emitted ONLY inside the transmit branch. Conclusion for this run: capture and timing were satisfied and the deficit is stored energy at the transmit step. Keep this as the standing localization; if a later run instead shows 'energy-threshold' or a missed contact step, the localization changes and the derivation below must be redone rather than patched.

DERIVATION PROCEDURE (re-executable, no parameter values supplied by the condition). Step 1: re-derive by direct stepping the recorded recurrence at the recorded dt_s, for each candidate parameter pair, rather than trusting a closed form. Step 2: use the closed-form bookkeeping only as a cross-check and as margin accounting, with n = ceil(tx_duration_s/dt_s), tx_j = output_v*tx_current_a*dt_s, eon = c*ready_v^2/2, eoff = c*off_v^2/2, emax = c*cap_voltage_max_v^2/2, giving the necessary pre-transmit store E*(c) = max(n*tx_j + eoff, (n-1)*tx_j + eon), the necessary capture condition eon <= E_avail(contact step) computed from the recorded source power, harvest efficiency and off power including the spill cap, and the completion and data-age tests completion <= deadline_s and completion - event_s <= max_data_age_s. Step 3: apply only these model-derived inequalities, each with an explicit fractional margin (require loaded_v >= output_v*(1+m), post-debit store >= eoff*(1+m), completion <= deadline_s - n*dt_s) and record the margin, so that a thin but positive margin is visible instead of being rounded into success. Two anti-over-exclusion rules are mandatory: (a) never exclude any grid point on a heuristic such as 'large capacitance is impractical' or 'a capacitor must be at least the full transmit energy'; the recorded inequalities are the only exclusions, and they typically bound an interval, not a point; (b) never treat a sufficient rule as necessary, i.e. a point that fails the closed form but steps the recurrence to an emitted frame counts as feasible evidence and must be recorded as a counterexample to the closed form.

SELECTION AND EXECUTION ORDER (budget-aware). Enumerate the legal grid (capacitance_f in [2.5e-5,1e-4], tx_not_before_s in [2,7] on the dt_s grid), keep points passing Step 3 with positive margin, rank by the minimum normalized margin, and pick the top-ranked point. Spend at most one candidate execution on it (recorded budget: 2 distinct designs / 2 candidate executions), then: if it emits exactly one valid frame of required_application_bytes with unique_frames satisfied and the deadline and max-data-age tests passing, record service completion and stop. If it does not, retain the returned trace, activity and packets verbatim as a counterexample, do not silently edit parameters, and either spend the one remaining execution on the next-ranked point from the same derived set or explicitly return no-update. No automatic retry, no re-seeding, no change to the model, task, evaluator or physical assumptions. Any claim beyond the observed single run (hardware behavior, statistical advantage, transfer to another task, recursive self-improvement) is out of scope and must be reported as UNKNOWN.

OBSERVATION POLICY. Retained artifacts contain actions but not per-step energies, so conclusions must cite the model law plus an executed trace, never the action log alone. Persist, per candidate: the executed pair, the derived E*, eon, eoff, emax, margins, the derived feasible set before execution, the full trace and packets, and an explicit UNKNOWN label wherever an input or a version hash is missing or changed. If a source version hash differs from the referenced ones, stop and re-derive from the new payload instead of reusing any number.

CONTEXT POLICY. Carry this procedure from task entry so that the localization, the derived set and the margins are available before any parameter is touched; after any coupled D execution, require complete feedback as stated above before the next decision, and if feedback is incomplete, return no-update rather than inferring the missing fields.

H_proposal.hypothesis: 上一轮失败（saved_activity: boot 1.316s, capture 2.0s, tx-start 2.0s, 2.001s brownout reason=tx-transient, packets=[]）不是时间窗问题，而是发射前储能不足以支撑多步负载：acquired model_law(b-transient-behavior-v1) 每个 dt 步先算 loaded_v=sqrt(2E/C)-esr*I 并要求 loaded_v>=Vout，再扣 draw=Vout*I*dt，然后要求剩余 E>=eoff=0.5*C*Voff^2，否则 reset 且 volatile 锁存清空 captured。当 tx_not_before 只由时间门（=event_s）触发时，发射从刚好够 boot 的低能态开始，第二/后续步的 pre-energy 低于 0.5*C*(Vout)^2 导致 loaded_v<Vout。故假设：给 H 增加一个‘先由模型律解析导出能量守卫、再选 C 与 tx_not_before’的可重复步骤，可在不修改任务/评估器/器件物理、且不越出合法区间的前提下，使程序能预先排除必然 brownout 的设计并定位可完成 2ms 发射的时间下限。
H_proposal.method_text:
【H 程序性更新：能量守卫优先的设计流程】本步骤仅为可重新执行的设计程序，不是器件指派、不是验收声明，也不修改任务/评估器/器件物理假设。

1) 先 acquire component_record、excitation_record、model_law、saved_activity，读取冻结常量：C、Vmax、Vready、Voff、Vout、tx_current_a(I)、tx_duration_s、esr、boot_j/boot_delay_s、idle/off_power、harvest_efficiency、source_segments 功率、dt_s、event_s、deadline_s、max_data_age_s、required_application_bytes、unique_frames，以及 tx_not_before_s 与 C 的合法区间。

2) 由 model_law 的 simulate_b 结构解析导出步进预算（符号形式，不写死数值）：L=ceil(tx_duration_s/dt)；draw=Vout*I*dt；eon=0.5*C*Vready^2；eoff=0.5*C*Voff^2；Emax=0.5*C*Vmax^2。每个 TX 步 k=1..L 需满足 pre_k >= 0.5*C*(Vout+esr*I)^2 且 pre_k-draw >= eoff。

3) 推出完整 2ms 级发射的最小发射前储能：E_req=(L-1)*draw + max(0.5*C*(Vout+esr*I)^2, draw+eoff)。并推出净充电速率 P_net=(sum source power)*harvest_efficiency - background((idle if powered else off) 取用)，把 E(t)=min(P_net*t, Emax)。

4) 可行性过滤：只保留 Emax>=E_req 的 C；不满足者记为 infeasible/unknown 并保留事实，不得伪造或强行发射。

5) 时间窗过滤：以 t_nb>=E_req/P_net 给出最早可发射时刻（若 E 触顶则由 Emax 维持），并要求 t_nb+L*dt <= min(deadline_s, event_s+max_data_age_s)；同时要求 boot 早于 event_s 且 P_net>0 保证捕获后无 brownout（volatile 锁存在无 reset 时保持），在合法 tx_not_before 区间内选择高于下限并留余量的值。

6) 回放核验：对每个候选设计用 model_law.simulate_b(或等价解析步进)回放，要求出现 >=1 个 packet、application_bytes=required_application_bytes、unique_frames=1，且 activity 中无 reason=tx-transient 的 brownout；否则判失败并保留真实 trace 与费用。

7) 预算内（至多2个 distinct designs）逐一执行；失败/未知/no-update 一律如实保留，禁止事后改任务或评估器来‘通过’，也不得把本程序等同于方法迁移、统计优势或 RSI。

8) 输出仅引用本次 acquire 的版本事实（source_sha256 与 saved_activity 动作）；不声明硬件或外部验收，验收在外部服务。

H_proposal.falsifier: Falsified on a fresh session from the same base H and sources if any of: (a) a legal design that satisfies the derived predicates of that session still browns out between capture and tx-complete, or still yields packets=[], or yields more or fewer than the one required frame; (b) a legal design that violates the capture-reachability predicate or the transmit-admissibility predicate still delivers the required frame by the deadline, i.e. one of the predicates is not necessary in this model; (c) the procedure cannot decide a case and the outcome would have to be guessed instead of reported UNKNOWN; (d) dt does not divide tx_duration_s, so N (and the final step's min(dt,tx_left)) is ambiguous and two derivations from the same sources predict different outcomes. Any one such observation retires the necessity claim for the offending predicate, while the ledger and source-binding steps stand. Scope of the claim is also invalidated if the latch variant changes to passive-mechanical (capture would survive a reset), if more than one contact window or a shunt appears, if esr_ohm or boot_j is nonzero and unread, if dt changes, or if the question is moved from the frozen digital model to physical hardware, where no calibration exists and the answer must stay UNKNOWN.
H_proposal.hypothesis: The retained failure (capture at the contact step, then brownout reason=tx-transient one step later, packets=[], no retry) is not an unlucky draw but the forced consequence of admitting transmit on capture alone. In the frozen b-transient-behavior-v1 model a request lasts N = tx_duration_s/dt model steps, and each of those steps independently requires pre-debit loaded_v >= output_v (equivalently stored energy >= C*output_v^2/2) and post-debit stored energy >= Eoff; the per-step debit q = output_v*tx_current_a*min(dt,tx_left) does not shrink with C while Emax and Eon do. Hence transmit is admissible only if the transmit-start energy e_T satisfies e_T >= max(C*output_v^2/2, C*off_v^2/2 + q) + (N-1)*(q - g), where g is the per-step net charge. Because the latch is volatile and the contact window is a single non-recurring step, any reset between capture and tx-complete is total loss of that episode, so 'powered and ready at the contact step' and 'the whole request completes without a reset' are one joint obligation, not two. An H that derives these predicates symbolically from the entry sources, screens the legal design space against them, lets transmit start later as a legitimate charge-accumulation lever, and keeps the infeasible boundary and the failed activity as counterexamples will predict the frozen model's per-design outcome (frame count, application bytes, deadline, brownout occurrence) without being handed any value.
H_proposal.method_text:
M-H, consumed from task entry. Every symbol below is read from the frozen sources at entry; no value is assumed and no value is pre-chosen.

STEP 0 - Bind sources, mark UNKNOWN. Read capacitance_f, cap_voltage_max_v, ready_v, off_v, cap_initial_voltage_v, event_latch, output_v, tx_current_a, tx_duration_s, esr_ohm, boot_j, boot_delay_s, harvest_efficiency, idle_power_w, off_power_w from component_record; dt_s, duration_s, event_s, contact_duration_s, source_segments, shunts from excitation_record; deadline_s, issued_s, single_query_only, nonce_sequence, the seq/key/event token, required_application_bytes from the task query_protocol; and the simulation semantics from model_law. Anything missing is UNKNOWN and must not be filled with a plausible number. Note explicitly that the model_law docstring describes an ideal passive-mechanical latch while the configured event_latch may be volatile: read the field, do not inherit the docstring assumption. Physical calibration, nonce cryptography and datasheet equivalence are out of scope and must never be claimed.

STEP 1 - Keep D and H separate. Capacitance and the transmit-not-before time are device edits (D). This procedure is H: it may not contain a chosen capacitance or a chosen transmit time, may not submit a device assignment as the method, and may not edit the task, the model, or the acceptance rule. Its only output is an admission test plus a derived feasible set that a later D step consumes.

STEP 2 - Build the per-step energy ledger at the model's dt, not an average-power budget. Thresholds on stored energy E: Emax = C*cap_voltage_max_v^2/2, Eon = C*ready_v^2/2, Eoff = C*off_v^2/2. Per-step net charge while idle: g = (sum of active source_segments power_w * harvest_efficiency - P_drain) * dt, with P_drain = off_power_w while unpowered and idle_power_w while powered; the switch is a discrete event, so bound both. Per-step transmit debit: q = output_v * tx_current_a * min(dt, tx_left). Read esr_ohm and boot_j rather than assuming them zero. A 'there is enough energy overall' heuristic is sufficient reasoning at best and must not be promoted into a feasibility exclusion; the model resets on a single step.

STEP 3 - Trace every event source to delivery before choosing values. (a) Capture: the powered capture branch fires only when powered, ready (t >= ready_at), and event_s <= t < event_s + contact_duration_s, so the window is ceil(contact_duration_s/dt) steps wide; the boot branch runs earlier in the same step, so a boot landing exactly on the contact step still captures. (b) Pending state: with a volatile latch, capture is cleared by every reset, and the contact window does not recur, so a reset after capture destroys that episode for good. (c) Delivery: a frame exists only at the step where tx_left reaches zero on a non-reset path; that packet is the service completion and nothing follows it - no retry and no second frame. Therefore treat 'powered and ready at the contact step' and 'the request runs to completion without any reset' as one joint obligation.

STEP 4 - State the admissibility predicates symbolically. P1 capture reachable: the first boot step is no later than the step containing event_s, with Eon compared against the net charge accumulated by that step. P2 hold: between capture and transmit start the device must stay at or above Eoff; stored energy rises in that interval, so the only bound is spill at Emax, which caps E but does not lose feasibility. P3 transmit admissible: with e_T the stored energy at the transmit-start step, every transmit step k = 0..N-1 requires pre-debit energy e_T - k*(q - g) >= C*output_v^2/2 (with the esr_ohm*tx_current_a term subtracted from loaded_v when esr is nonzero) and post-debit energy >= Eoff; N = tx_duration_s/dt is valid only when dt divides tx_duration_s, otherwise the final step's min(dt, tx_left) and the tx_left tolerance make N uncertain - record UNKNOWN. P4 deadline: the completing step occurs no later than min(deadline_s, event_s + max_data_age_s). P5 frame: exactly one frame carrying required_application_bytes, with the seq/key/event token already fixed by the model, so de-duplication or nonce machinery is not part of the fix and must not be proposed as one. P6 reachability of e_T: e_T <= Emax and e_T <= g*t at the chosen start time, so the earliest admissible start is the smallest t >= max(event_s, transmit-not-before) with g*t >= the required e_T; extra wait raises e_T up to Emax. Consequence to state openly: 'transmit as early as possible' is not a safe default, and a later transmit time is a legitimate lever.

STEP 5 - Derive a feasible set, not a point. Eliminate the legal ranges against P1-P6 and keep the feasible region together with its infeasible boundary as evidence. Preserve the derived non-monotonicity in capacitance: q is fixed by output_v and tx_current_a and does not shrink with C, while Emax and Eon do, so too small a C cannot hold roughly two transmit debits and too large a C boots after the single contact step; the safe direction is not monotone and both edges are real. If the feasible set is empty or touchable only at a boundary, report UNKNOWN / no-update instead of forcing a design.

STEP 6 - Preregister order and margin under the candidate budget. Predict each candidate's outcome from Steps 2-4 before running it, run at most the budgeted number of distinct designs, and make the first candidate sit strictly inside the derived region and the second probe the edge whose predicate is least sure. Label the interior margin as a robustness heuristic only: boundary designs remain feasible and are recorded, never excluded from the feasible space on heuristic grounds. After each observation, compare the actual activity and packet record against the prediction and record the mismatch.

STEP 7 - Keep failures as counterexamples. Retain the observation with capture, a tx-transient brownout on the next step, packets=[], and a late reboot as a standing counterexample proving capture-then-reset is unrecoverable under a volatile latch with one contact window; cite it whenever a later design re-asserts that capturing is sufficient. Never overwrite it, and never report a completed service the trace does not contain.

STEP 8 - Claim discipline. Report only the derived predicates and feasible region, the frozen model's predicted outcome for the designs actually run, and retained observations with their real brownout and energy costs. Do not claim hardware behaviour, statistical advantage, transfer to other tasks, or any recursive self-improvement; leave acceptance to the independent service.

H_proposal.falsifier: The update is falsified if, on the same frozen task, sources and budget, a candidate that passes the gate with the stated margins (energy margin >= the declared safety factor at every step of the retention interval, loaded-voltage margin >= the declared mV floor at the final tx step, no spill loss counted as usable energy) still yields no valid 8-byte frame, or suffers a brownout anywhere in the declared retention interval; or if a candidate that violates a declared inequality (and was therefore rejected) nonetheless yields a valid frame inside the deadline. It is also falsified if the gate's margin ordering inverts against observed outcomes, or if the two budgeted candidates fail with a signature traceable to a term the gate did not model (e.g. spill, boot cost, ready delay, per-step load re-test) - that shows the screening is incomplete rather than the apparatus being unmodelled.
H_proposal.hypothesis: The retained base failure is a screening defect in H, not a missing parameter value: the base run captured the event (contact 0-0.008 s, captures 0.0037-0.0079 s) and then lost it via a brownout at 0.0121 s whose own record carries event_was_captured=true, with zero packets; the post-event power window at 0.0381 s shows event_captured=false. Under a volatile latch this is irreversible loss, so any procedure that selects a design without first debiting every shunt and dark-gap drain inside the interval [first capture, tx-complete] cannot distinguish feasible from infeasible designs. Hypothesis: adding an explicit, closed-form feasibility gate (retention interval + per-step loaded-voltage test + running energy debit + stated safety margin) to H before any candidate execution is spent makes predicted feasibility agree with the observed transient behaviour on this frozen apparatus, and makes failures diagnosable by named term instead of by re-tuning parameters.
H_proposal.method_text:
PROCEDURE H: feasibility-gated candidate selection for the frozen battery-free task (v2).

Scope and hard limits. Use only the frozen sources (component_record, excitation_record, saved_activity, model_law) and the frozen legal ranges capacitance_f in [4e-6, 2.2e-5], tx_not_before_s in [0, 0.045]. Do not modify the task, the excitation, the model law or any acceptance rule; do not assert acceptance - only host-side service decides. Budget: at most 2 candidate executions / 2 distinct designs; never silently retry; unknown, failure and no-update outcomes are recorded as observed, with actual costs.

Step 1 - read the retention semantics before choosing anything. From component_record.event_latch decide the latch class. If the latch is volatile, state explicitly: a capture is retained only while the device stays powered, so the design must hold power continuously from the first capture through tx-complete; any energy-threshold or tx-transient brownout in that interval destroys the event and the contact window (event_s .. event_s + contact_duration_s) may already be closed, making the loss unrecoverable. Check saved_activity for brownout rows with event_was_captured=true and for empty packets; treat those as latch-loss evidence, not as a low-energy tweak.

Step 2 - transcribe the discrete evaluation order from model_law as an explicit ledger, one row per dt step, in this order: harvest_j = source_w*dt*harvest_efficiency; spill_j = max(0, e - emax); background_j = min(e, idle_power_w*dt while powered else off_power_w*dt); shunt_j = min(e, sum of shunt energy in the step); then, per step, eoff-crossing test (brownout), eon-crossing test (boot, minus boot_j, ready_at = t + boot_delay_s), contact test only when powered and t >= ready_at, tx-start only when captured and t >= tx_not_before_s, and inside tx the per-step load test loaded_v = sqrt(2e/C) - esr_ohm*tx_current_a must stay >= output_v with requested = output_v*tx_current_a*min(dt, tx_left) debited each step, re-tested against the remaining energy, and the step also fails if e < eoff. Note that emax = C*cap_voltage_max_v^2/2 caps useful storage, so harvest beyond emax is not bankable energy.

Step 3 - write the feasibility conditions as closed-form inequalities in the design parameters alone, before any execution: (a) first power-on time from the first source segment versus the contact window; (b) capture existence: does [boot + boot_delay_s, contact end] intersect a powered interval; (c) retention interval: cumulative energy over [first capture, tx-complete] after debiting all harvest, all shunts inside that interval, all background drain, any boot_j, and the full tx demand (output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s), never below eoff and never below the per-step load-test energy floor C*(output_v + esr_ohm*tx_current_a)^2/2 evaluated with the energy already spent; (d) last-step margin: the same loaded-voltage test at the final tx step with the energy remaining then; (e) completion time <= deadline_s with exactly one 8-byte frame; (f) rule out designs whose first power-on lands after the contact window, since with a volatile latch no later power window can ever produce the frame.

Step 4 - rank, do not tune. For each legal candidate compute each inequality's normalized margin (available/required), take the minimum, and require a declared safety factor before accepting a candidate (declare it in the record, e.g. >=1.2x on energy and >=50 mV on loaded voltage). Reject any candidate whose binding constraint sits within the noise of the model. Prefer the candidate whose binding constraint is not the retention interval if a choice exists, since the retention term is the one the base run got wrong.

Step 5 - spend the budget deliberately. With at most 2 designs, use the two experiments to discriminate rather than to nudge: one design that maximises retention margin (largest stored energy at capture relative to the full post-capture debit set), and one that minimises the retention interval (earliest legal tx start after capture completes). Do not re-run the base design. Record both outcomes, including no packet, with the observed brownout reasons and the trace terms that dominated.

Step 6 - diagnose by term, not by retreat. If a candidate fails, compare the observed per-step start_j/stored_j/harvest_j/spill_j/background_j/shunt_j/tx_j against the ledger prediction at the same step. A mismatch identifies a missing or misordered term; fix that term in the ledger and record it as an unknown. Do not edit the model, task or evaluator, and do not fabricate an acceptance claim. If the two candidates fail with the same signature, report no-update for this cycle rather than emitting a third guess.

Step 7 - reporting discipline. Report hypothesis, ledger inequalities with declared margins, the chosen design parameters, the actual observed outcome and cost, and the explicit unknowns (e.g. physical calibration, behaviour outside the frozen source segments). Do not claim hardware validity, statistical advantage, transfer of the method or recursive self-improvement; this is a one-shot procedural revision on a fixed task, and the parameter choice itself is a later design decision, not part of this H.

H_proposal.falsifier: The H scope is invalidated by any of: (1) any trace in which a packet with application_bytes=8 exists although the activity list shows a reset (brownout with event_was_captured=true, or a tx-transient reset) strictly between the last capture and tx-start - then capture continuity is not the binding mechanism and M2 is wrong; (2) for the same inputs as the retained failure (C=1e-5, tx_not_before_s=0.045) a packet appearing - then the post-shunt/deadline arithmetic in M3 excluded a feasible point; (3) a candidate that satisfies every M1-M3 inequality yet returns packets=[] with a triage label outside {no-ready-in-window, reset-cleared-capture, tx-transient-sag, deadline-overflow} - then the chain enumeration is incomplete; (4) predicted first_boot_s or first capture time off by more than about 2*dt=2e-4 s without any source or parameter change - then the phase budgets are mis-derived; (5) evidence that a brownout with event_was_captured=false is followed by a capture outside the contact window - then 'capture only inside contact duration' is misread and the chain is mis-ordered. H_proposal.hypothesis: Under the frozen b-transient-behavior-v1 apparatus with event_latch=volatile (component_record), success is governed by the continuity of the chain capture -> no reset -> tx-start(t>=tx_not_before_s) -> 20 TX steps -> tx-complete(<=deadline), not by peak stored energy or by deferring TX to the latest allowed instant. The retained failed trace is consistent only with a broken middle link, not with an energy shortage: capture is logged at 3.7-7.9 ms while powered/ready inside the 0-8 ms contact window, the 12.1 ms brownout is logged with event_was_captured=true (40 uJ shunt at 12 ms plus the source-free 6-30 ms gap pushed e under eoff=C*1.8^2/2), the volatile latch then reads event_was_captured=false at the 38.1 ms reboot, and by then the contact window has closed, so `captured` can never be re-set and the tx-start guard never fires: packets=[] at any tx_not_before. Prediction to be tested by the next candidate execution(s): the closed-form phase arithmetic (charge rates 0.01498 W unpowered / 0.0031 W powered in the 30-60 ms segment / -0.0002 W idle, shunt 4e-5 J at 12 ms, eon=C*2.8^2/2, eoff=C*1.8^2/2, emax=C*3.3^2/2, sag sqrt(2e/C)>=1.8+0.3*0.008=1.8024 V, TX charge 1.8*0.008*0.002=2.88e-5 J) reproduces the observed first_boot_s, first capture time, reset time and reason, and packet presence/absence for both continuity families; and that a TX co-located with the capture window yields a packet without ever crossing the 12 ms shunt while the deferred family requires e(post-12 ms shunt) and e(30 ms) both stay above eoff, which at C=1e-5 is arithmetically impossible (emax-eoff=C*(3.3^2-1.8^2)/2=C*3.825=3.83e-5 J < 4e-5 J shunt plus drain). H_proposal.method_text:
H METHOD - consumed from task entry, before any device choice. It reasons about the frozen apparatus and does not edit the task, the model, the ranges, the hooks or the evaluator. It does not select or submit a device: a (C, tx_not_before_s) pair is a separate D decision whose acceptance is decided externally. Physical calibration is UNKNOWN; the model is an assumption record, not hardware truth.

M0. Bind inputs. component_record (id 260, event_latch=volatile, boot_j=5e-6 J, boot_delay_s=1e-3, off_v=1.8, ready_v=2.8, cap_voltage_max_v=3.3, output_v=1.8, tx_current_a=0.008, tx_duration_s=2e-3, esr=0.3 ohm, harvest_efficiency=0.9, idle_power_w=2e-4, off_power_w=2e-5, cap_initial_voltage_v=0). excitation_record (dt=1e-4 s, event_s=0, contact_duration_s=0.008, deadline_s=0.1, duration_s=1, sources 0-0.006 s at 1.6666667e-2 W and 0.03-0.06 s at 3.6666667e-3 W, shunt 4e-5 J at 0.012 s). model_law b-transient-behavior-v1. Budget: 2 candidate executions, 2 distinct designs.

M1. Derive, per candidate C, before any run: eon=C*ready_v^2/2; eoff=C*off_v^2/2; emax=C*cap_voltage_max_v^2/2; usable margin emax-eoff=C*(3.3^2-1.8^2)/2=C*3.825; sag requirement sqrt(2e/C)>=output_v+esr*tx_current_a=1.8024 V, i.e. e>=C*1.6243 J; TX charge=output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s=2.88e-5 J, drawn as 1.44e-6 J/step over tx_duration_s/dt=20 steps. TX per-step demand (1.44e-6 J) is below the phase-A per-step harvest (1.5e-6 J), so during an active source segment TX is nearly energy-neutral; it is only the source-free segments that make TX a net drain.

M2. Write the response chain explicitly and never collapse it. A packet exists only if all links hold: (a) contact window W=[event_s, event_s+contact_duration_s)=[0,0.008) s; (b) a step sets captured only if powered AND t>=ready_at AND t in W (capture event); (c) every reset clears captured because the latch is volatile (reset paths: end-of-step e<eoff; TX step with loaded_v<output_v or e<eoff), so a capture event is evidence of (b) only and is NOT evidence that pending state survives a reset; (d) tx-start requires captured at that step AND t>=tx_not_before_s; (e) tx-complete requires 20 consecutive TX steps with no reset; (f) t_complete<=deadline_s. Hence the requirement is the conjunction: exists t_c in W with (powered, ready) at t_c, AND no reset on [t_c, t_complete], AND t_start>=tx_not_before_s, AND t_complete<=0.1 s. Check each link separately and record which one fails first.

M3. Source-bound budgets per phase (formulas, then numbers for the candidate): phase A [0,0.006): net while unpowered =0.9*1.6666667e-2-2e-5=1.498e-2 W, so t_boot~eon/1.498e-2 (plus one-step quantization, then minus boot_j=5e-6) and ready_at=t_boot+1e-3; phase G [0.006,0.03): net=-idle_power_w=-2e-4 W, no harvest; shunt at 0.012 s: e<-e-min(e,4e-5); phase B [0.03,0.06): net=0.9*3.6666667e-3-2e-4=3.1e-3 W; TX steps: e<-e+harvest_step-1.44e-6. Evaluate and report in J, noting sign: (i) spill at emax in phase A; (ii) e just after the 12 ms shunt vs eoff; (iii) minimum e over phase G; (iv) e at tx-start vs eoff+net TX charge; (v) t_complete vs deadline. Two branch conditions follow and must both be shown, not assumed: an F1 (co-located) run needs t_ready<0.008 s and, if the source is active across TX, near-neutral energy plus the sag inequality; if TX would extend past 0.006 s it needs emax-eoff>=2.88e-5 + idle drain over that span, i.e. C*3.825>=~2.92e-5 -> C>=~7.6e-6 F. An F2 (deferred) run, e.g. tx_not_before_s=0.045, needs e(post-shunt)>eoff and e(0.03 s)>eoff, i.e. C*3.825>4e-5+~4.8e-6 -> C>~1.17e-5 F, plus t_ready<0.008 s. For C=1e-5, C*3.825=3.83e-5 J<4e-5 J, so any capture obtained in W is arithmetically lost at the 12 ms shunt and F2 is dead on that branch - this is a number, not a preference; at larger C both branches survive and must be compared on margin.

M4. Never convert a sufficient heuristic into a necessary exclusion. 'Charge to emax and transmit at the latest permitted time' maximizes stored energy yet is exactly the shape that loses a volatile capture when the shunt plus the source-free gap force e<eoff between capture and tx-start; it is therefore sufficient-looking, not sufficient. Conversely 'transmit immediately at capture' is not universally available: it needs t_ready inside the contact window and either an active source across the 20 TX steps or emax-eoff>=2.88e-5 J. Enumerate both families, keep a family only when the M1-M3 numbers hold, prefer the family with fewer coupled links and larger J margins, and reject a design only on a failed inequality or a contradicting trace - never on 'less stored energy must be worse'.

M5. Experiment order under the 2-execution / 2-distinct-design budget: spend the slots on distinct designs, one probe per family, and never run the same design twice as a retry. Probe F1 first (one phase, no shunt or gap crossing, largest margins); evaluate F2 only if F1 is rejected by its trace, and if F2 is tried, check the post-shunt margin first because it is the knife-edge at high C. Before each run, write the predicted t_boot, t_c, t_start, t_complete and the post-shunt margin; a run whose prediction disagrees is the more informative outcome and must be kept, not rerun.

M6. Observation policy: read back the complete response (activity, first_boot_s, packets, and the trace fields stored_j, voltage_v, loaded_v, powered, contact, event_captured, shunt_j, spill_j). Record first boot time, every capture, every brownout with its reason and event_was_captured, tx-start/tx-complete, packets[].hex and application_bytes. Assign exactly one failure-triage label per run, in chain order: no-ready-in-window | reset-cleared-capture (cite brownout time and event_was_captured) | tx-transient-sag (cite loaded_v) | deadline-overflow. Pass the label and its J/s numbers into the next design choice; do not repeat an identical design.

M7. Claim and retention discipline. Eight application bytes with unique_frames=1 in packets is a candidate completion; validity is decided by the external service, not here. If packets=[], report service as not completed and name the broken link. Keep the retained failure as evidence: saved_activity has packets=[], capture 3.7-7.9 ms, brownout 0.0121 s with event_was_captured=true, second boot 0.0381 s, later brownout with event_was_captured=false - i.e. a capture existed but pending state did not survive the reset, and re-capture was impossible after the window closed. Preserve UNKNOWN (physical calibration, any unrun design) and actual cost (<=2 candidate executions, no native dispatches). No automatic retries; no claim of hardware validation, statistical advantage, method transfer or RSI.

H_proposal.hypothesis: Retained failure is a window-accounting error, not a tuning error. At the base design (C=1e-5 F, tx_not_before_s at its range maximum 0.045 s) the volatile latch captured during the only contact window (event_s=0 to event_s+contact_duration_s=0.008 s; captures observed 0.0037-0.0079 s) and then lost that capture at the 0.012 s shunt (4e-5 J) via an energy-threshold brownout at 0.0121 s; the retry at 0.0381 s falls in the second, weaker source segment (0.003667 W from 0.03-0.06 s) after the 0.006-0.03 s dark gap, decays to off_v by 0.2512 s, and emits zero packets. The wait-and-transmit-late reading of tx_not_before_s assumes capture survives brownouts; under a volatile latch the correct object is a single uninterrupted powered interval that must contain capture, the full TX burst (output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s), and completion before any shunt, source-gap collapse, or deadline. Procedure improvement: make that interval inequality the gate every candidate must pass before an execution slot is spent, and stop treating bounded design knobs as defaults-at-range-max. Prediction under the current H baseline: candidate designs are being chosen without any stated window inequality, so the retained zero-packet outcome recurs or succeeds only by luck.
H_proposal.method_text:
H (procedural) update, applied before any candidate design is executed. It changes how the design procedure reads the frozen facts and spends its two candidate execution slots; it does not fix device parameter values.

1. Window enumeration first (observation_policy). Before proposing any candidate, write out, in seconds, the ordered constraint set taken from the acquired sources: the contact interval [event_s, event_s+contact_duration_s]; every source segment as [start_s, end_s] with its power, plus every dark gap between segments; every shunt time and its energy; the deadline; and dt. Label which of these are reset-capable (they can force stored energy below off_v) and which are only energy sources. Quote the source ids and hashes the numbers came from.

2. Latch-lifetime obligation (skills). Read event_latch from component_record and state the retention rule in words. If the latch is volatile, record that any reset (energy threshold, transmit-transient voltage floor, or a shunt/dark-gap decay) clears the capture, so the design must be judged on a single powered interval: capture, then transmit burst, then completion, with no reset in between and completion before the earliest later reset-capable event and before the deadline. If the latch is passive-mechanical, note the weaker obligation instead. Also derive, from component_record only, the per-frame transmit energy and the loaded-voltage floor needed to stay off the transmit-transient reset.

3. Feasibility envelope, then ranking (experiment_order). Compute, within the legal design ranges only, the interval inequality from steps 1-2 and record which parameter region satisfies it. Treat every bounded parameter as constrained by that inequality: any value placed at a range endpoint, and especially at the maximum-delay endpoint, must carry an explicit window reason; 'wait longer for stability' is not such a reason when the latch is volatile. Rank candidate designs by margin to the nearest reset-capable event and to the deadline, not by nominal stored energy at peak. Only then execute; spend the two available candidate executions on designs that differ in the constraint-relevant parameter identified here, and pre-register what observation would reject each one.

4. Consistency check by replay (observation_policy). Before executing, replay the retained saved_activity against the envelope in steps 1-2 using the recorded settings and the acquired model law, and require agreement on first boot time, on the first brownout relative to the shunt, and on the empty packet list. Report disagreement as a retained unknown rather than silently rescaling assumptions. Never edit the task, the excitation record, the model law, or the ranges to make a candidate fit.

5. Reporting discipline (global_prompt). For each candidate, report the stated inequalities, the observed events with timestamps, the packet list (including empty), and any no-update or failure as retained. Do not claim acceptance, hardware validity, statistical advantage, or method transfer: qualification and independent service are external, and physical calibration is UNKNOWN. If the envelope cannot discriminate among candidates, return no-update rather than adding rules.

H_proposal.method_text:
Procedural H consumed from task entry. It changes reasoning and observation order only. It is NOT a device assignment, NOT an acceptance decision, and it does not edit the task, model_law, evaluator, or legal ranges.

Step 0 - keep D and H separate. A device edit D sets numeric design fields (capacitance_f, tx_not_before_s) inside the legal ranges. This H emits no parameter values, no device, and no service label. Every event below is traced source -> capture -> reset -> delivery; a completed transmission is not evidence that pending state survives a later reset.

Step 1 - build the source-bound energy ledger before touching any design, from the actually acquired sources:
  eon = 0.5*C*ready_v^2 ; eoff = 0.5*C*off_v^2 ; emax = 0.5*C*cap_voltage_max_v^2  (component_record, for the C under test)
  E_boot = boot_j ; E_tx = output_v*tx_current_a*tx_duration_s
  background per step = (idle_power_w if powered else off_power_w)*dt  (dt from excitation_record)
  harvest per step = sum over source_segments overlapping the step of power_w*harvest_efficiency
  subtract every shunts[*].energy_j at its time_s; spill above emax is loss, not stored energy.
Compute the minimum stored energy at TX start e_min_start such that all TX steps finish with e >= eoff AND loaded_v = sqrt(2*e/C) - esr_ohm*tx_current_a >= output_v. Record e_min_start as an interval [e_min_start, emax], not a single 'best late' time. With the acquired component_record this is eoff + E_tx plus an esr/tx_current correction; derive it each run, do not hard-code it.

Step 2 - bound capture lifetime by the latch fact. Read event_latch. If it is 'volatile', capture ends at the FIRST reset after capture; a reset for any reason (energy-threshold or tx-transient) discards the event. From the ledger compute the earliest post-capture reset time (driven by shunts, source gaps, background, boot_j, and any TX-started-but-unaffordable transient) and keep it as a hard upper bound on tx-complete. If it is 'passive-mechanical', do not import the volatile bound; state which branch was taken. UNKNOWN latch value => stop and report UNKNOWN.

Step 3 - derive the admissible TX-start window instead of a heuristic:
  lo = max(ready_at, first capture step, earliest step with e >= e_min_start)
  hi = min(first post-capture reset time, deadline_s) - tx_duration_s
Prefer the earliest energy-sufficient start. A heuristic that 'wait for the later source segment' (or for any specific late time) may be sufficient in one world but must not be used to exclude a feasible earlier window: sufficiency is not a necessary-feasibility exclusion.

Step 4 - if lo > hi, return UNKNOWN / no candidate; never submit a candidate whose only success path assumes capture retention across a reset. Preserve the failed activity and the falsifying trace side by side rather than overwriting them.

Step 5 - re-execute and check complete responses per candidate: (a) packets exist with application_bytes == required_application_bytes (8) and exactly unique_frames=1 distinct frame; (b) tx-complete occurs before the first post-capture reset; (c) no brownout with event_was_captured=true lies between capture and tx-complete; (d) final delivery time is within deadline_s. If ledger prediction and the model_law simulation disagree, the simulation is authoritative for observation and both are retained as a counterexample.

Step 6 - scope and honesty. This H is validated only against the frozen public-development packet (full_public_facts_sha256 49b3e48b...). Physical calibration stays UNKNOWN. Do not claim hardware behavior, statistical advantage, method migration, or RSI from these traces, and do not treat a passing trace as external service acceptance.
